top_choice_rationale: P001 (Chetty, Hendren, Friedman) is the only slate proposal that scores well on all four criteria I apply: originality, identification quality, durability and attribution tractability. It created a new empirical object, place-specific mobility measured on population administrative records. Its mover and childhood-exposure designs can be inspected and re-run by others, and the measurement standard has already been taken up with other registers. The three names are the recurring lead unit. Maturity is the main cost, because the core work dates from about 2014 to 2022. That cost applies mostly to long-run causal place-effect claims, and a citation limited to measurement and exposure-based designs avoids resting on them. P003 is second because it is the most mature and its credit is concentrated, but its cross-country identification is weaker. P002 is third. Kiyotaki and Moore are a clean pair, but marginal novelty relative to the 2022 prize and the indirect aggregate evidence count against it. P004 is fourth because its eight-name attribution cannot be resolved by a three-name cap and the micro price evidence only partly supports Calvo-style pricing. I rank no award last because every proposal on the slate rewards a substantive contribution. This ordering rests on general knowledge and the supplied files, not on independent verification.
recusal_note: No co-authorship or institutional tie to Chetty, Hendren, Friedman, Persson, Tabellini, Besley, Kiyotaki, Moore, Calvo, Taylor or Woodford is apparent from my profile. I co-authored the IJIO 2026 menu-cost paper with chair John Hassler and former chair Tore Ellingsen. That paper is adjacent to the price-rigidity theme of P004, which I rank fourth. My industrial-organisation background may make me favour method contributions that estimate something from data. My spouse's public political role is a public fact with no apparent bearing on any candidate. These are disclosures only, and I have completed the ballot.
